_purpose: Preregistered decision rules and search budgets (plan: 'Statistics and preregistration'). Fixed BEFORE the first training run. MUST NOT be revised after any arm has been launched.

falsification_rule.test: arm A vs arm B degradation slopes
falsification_rule.procedure: Fit R(delta) per seed (regret = 1 - success_once, and separately mean final distance to slot), extract the slope per seed by ordinary least squares over the delta grid, compare slope distributions.
falsification_rule.rule: If the 95% CIs of s_base and s_treat overlap, the effect is absent and that IS the reported result. Interpolation, extrapolation and composition grid points are fitted and reported separately, never averaged.
falsification_rule.note: B's one-step and latent targets are reported alongside; a one-step null alone is explained by BYOL-gamma and does not falsify.

lambda_sweep.coupling_metric: corr over lambda of probe R^2 for c (k) against negative degradation slope (-s)

test_d_budget.rule: Exactly 12 configurations per substitution arm, identical count across arms. No configuration may be added, removed, or re-run with different hyperparameters after launch. Each configuration runs the SAME seeds (0-4).
test_d_budget.closing_criterion: A substitution closes the gap iff |s_sub - s_treat| < epsilon with epsilon = 0.25 * |s_base - s_treat|, where s_base and s_treat are the main-arm mean slopes (10 seeds, multistep target, 1e4 data scale). Equivalently: the substitution must cover at least 75% of the A-to-B slope gap.

outcome_table.shuf_matches_treat: Not dynamics; a second head suffices.
outcome_table.shuf_matches_base_and_k_s_decoupled: A mechanism not on the list.

amendment_2026_08_17_test_c_interpretati.context: Recorded BEFORE any study arm was launched. The probe/ablation calibration tier measured that linear (single-direction and 16-dim INLP subspace) erasure cannot remove a redundantly/nonlinearly encoded quantity from trained features: the erased quantity remained decodable and the erasure impaired control no more than an equal-dimension random subspace, while the dummy negative control was exactly null.
amendment_2026_08_17_test_c_interpretati.rule: Test C (probe-then-ablate) results are interpreted asymmetrically: a POSITIVE differential effect (ablating the c-subspace degrades the slope substantially more than the random-subspace control) is evidence for M1; a NULL differential is UNINFORMATIVE about M1 and must not be counted as evidence against it. Erasure power (post-erasure ridge and MLP probe R^2) is reported alongside every ablation.
amendment_2026_08_17_test_c_interpretati.ablation_method: INLP subspace erasure (max 16 dims, ridge, r2_stop 0.05) with equal-dimension random orthonormal subspace control, per dynmod/analysis/probes.py
